rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may show mercy by ending the retribution that had fallen on the Israelites.
rows.anchor: يعني مما حل بكم من الانتقام منكم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: If they returned to wrongdoing, God would return to punishment; they did, and believers would humble them through tribute and warfare until the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: فبعث الله عليهم المؤمنين يذلونهم بالجزية والمحاربة إلى يوم القيامة

rows.speaker: بعض الصالحين
rows.claim: Alternatively, if they returned to obedience, God would return to acceptance.
rows.anchor: إن عدتم إلى الطاعة عدنا إلى القبول , قاله بعض الصالحين

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Hell as a حصير is a spread-out bed or resting place, from the word for a laid-out mat.
rows.anchor: يعني فراشا ومهادا , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Alternatively, Hell is a prison in which they are confined; حصير derives from confinement.
rows.anchor: حبسا يحبسون فيه , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: The poet's use of حصير for a king supports the sense of one enclosed by a screen or barrier.
rows.anchor: لأنه بالحجاب محصور , قال لبيد

none: The segment contains only an opening brace and no commentary.

rows.speaker: الكلبي والفراء
rows.claim: One interpretation of the Quran's guidance is the testimony that there is no god but God.
rows.anchor: أن لا إله إلا الله , قاله الكلبي والفراء

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Quran guides through its commands and prohibitions, which are the soundest course.
rows.anchor: ما تضمه من الأوامر والنواهي التي هي أصوب , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that a person seeks immediate benefit through harm that will return to hurt him in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: أن يطلب النفع في العاجل بالضر العائد عليه في الآجل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that people curse themselves or their children with death; if such a curse were answered like a good prayer, they would perish.
rows.anchor: أحدهم على نفسه أو ولده بالهلاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد
rows.claim: Human haste refers to people hastily praying against themselves, their children, or what concerns them.
rows.anchor: وما يخصه , وهذا قول ابن عباس وقتادة ومجاهد

rows.speaker: إبراهيم والضحاك
rows.claim: Alternatively, the verse refers to Adam, who hurried to rise when the spirit had reached his navel.
rows.anchor: حتى بلغت إلى سرته فأراد أن ينهض عجلا , وهذا قول إبراهيم والضحاك

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The erased sign of night is its darkness, in which paths cannot be seen, like writing erased from a book; al-Mawardi calls this especially eloquent.
rows.anchor: الطرقات كما لا نبصر ما محي من الكتاب , وهذا من أحسن البلاغة , وهو معنى قول ابن عباس

rows.speaker: علي وقتادة
rows.claim: Alternatively, the erased night sign is the dark mark on the moon, making its light weaker than the sun and distinguishing night from day.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول علي وقتادة ليكون ضوء القمر أقل من ضوء الشمس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The daylight sign may mean the sun that illuminates the eyes.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنها الشمس مضيئة للأبصار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the daylight sign means that it awakens people.
rows.anchor: أنها الشمس مضيئة للأبصار . الثاني : موقظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of each person's طائر is his good or bad deeds, likened to Arab omens from birds passing on the right or left.
rows.anchor: ألزمناه عمله من خير أو شر مثل ما كانت العرب تقوله

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Alternatively, طائره means a person's allotted fortune or share, as in the Arab expression for a سهم that falls to someone.
rows.anchor: من قول العرب : طار سهم فلان إذا خرج سهمه ونصيبه منه , قاله أبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opened record is the record of the person's good or bad deeds represented by his طائر.
rows.anchor: يعني كتاب طائره الذي في عنقه من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The record may be spread out to hasten good news for good deeds and rebuke for bad ones.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : تعجيلا للبشرى بالحسنة , والتوبيخ بالسيئة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, its being spread out publicly displays the person's deeds, good or bad.
rows.anchor: إظهار عمله من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to read may intensify reproach and rebuke through the person's reading of the record.
rows.anchor: لما في قراءته من زيادة التقريع والتوبيخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, reading makes the person acknowledge his own deeds against himself.
rows.anchor: ليكون إقراره بقراءته على نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حسيبا may mean that the person is a witness against himself.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : يعني شاهدا . والثاني : يعني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, حسيبا means that the person judges his own deeds, good or bad.
rows.anchor: الثاني : يعني حاكما بعملك من خير أو شر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has dealt fairly by making each person account for himself through his own deeds.
rows.anchor: ولقد أنصفك من جعلك حسيبا على نفسك بعملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Guidance benefits the guided person through the reward of obedience.
rows.anchor: يعني لما يحصل له من ثواب طاعته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Misguidance harms the person through the punishment of disobedience.
rows.anchor: يعني لما يحصل عليه من عقاب معصيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation is that no one is held accountable for another person's sin.
rows.anchor: أحدها : لا يؤاخذ أحد بذنب غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another explanation is that one person may not commit a sin on behalf of another person's sin.
rows.anchor: الثاني : لا يجوز لأحد أن يعصى لمعصية غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that nobody incurs another person's sin.
rows.anchor: الثالث : لا يأثم أحد بإثم غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A possible fourth explanation is that no one bears another's sin in a way that removes the perpetrator's own liability.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل رابعا : أن لا يتحمل أحد ذنب غيره ويسقط مأثمه عن فاعله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the view that reason precedes revealed law, punishment for religious ordinances waits for a messenger to explain them.
rows.anchor: على الشرائع الدينية حتى نبعث رسولا مبينا , وهذا قول من زعم أن العقل تقدم الشرع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the view that reason and revelation came together, no sin is punished until a messenger calls people to faith.
rows.anchor: على شيء من المعاصي حتى نبعث رسولا داعيا , وهذا قول من زعم أن العقل والشرع جاءا معا

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The threatened punishment may be the punishment of the afterlife, which is the apparent sense of Qatada's view.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : عذاب الآخرة . وهو ظاهر قول قتادة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may mean worldly punishment through annihilation of a people.
rows.anchor: الثاني : عذاب بالاستئصال في الدنيا ، وهو قول مقاتل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading of God's intending a town's destruction is intending to decree that it be destroyed.
rows.anchor: معناه إذا أردنا أن نحكم بهلاك قرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reads the phrase as 'when We destroy a town,' treating أردنا as an extra connective, as in 18:77.
rows.anchor: صلة زائدة كهي في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third interpretation is that destruction means the best people perish while the worst remain.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد بهلاك القرية فناء خيارها وبقاء شرارها

rows.speaker: الأئمة السبعة من القراء
rows.claim: The seven canonical readers pronounce أمرنا with a shortened, light mīm.
rows.anchor: الذي عليه الأئمة السبعة من القراء أن أمرنا مقصور مخفف

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: On one interpretation of the light form, God commanded the town's affluent people to obey, but they disobeyed.
rows.anchor: أي فعصوا بالمخالفة , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: هارون
rows.claim: A second interpretation of the light form is that God sent the town's arrogant leaders against it.
rows.anchor: الثاني : معناه : بعثنا مستكبريها , قاله هارون

rows.speaker: أبي
rows.claim: In Ubayy's reading, God sent the leading criminals of the town.
rows.anchor: وهي في قراءة أبي : بعثنا أكابر مجرميها

rows.speaker: أبو عثمان النهدي
rows.claim: With a doubled mīm, the reading means that God made the affluent people rulers with power.
rows.anchor: ومعناه جعلناهم أمراء مسلطين , قاله أبو عثمان النهدي

rows.speaker: الحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: With a lengthened initial alif, the reading means that God increased their numbers; the numerous then need an emir to direct them.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول الحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A Prophetic saying uses the relevant word to mean abundant offspring, illustrating increase in number.
rows.anchor: قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم ( خير المال مهرة

rows.speaker: لبيد
rows.claim: Labid's verse provides poetic evidence for the abundance sense of the lengthened reading.
rows.anchor:
وقال لبيد :
إن يغبطوا يهبطوا وإن أمروا

rows.speaker: السن
rows.claim: مترفيها may mean the town's tyrants.
rows.anchor: أحدها جباروها , قاله السن

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: مترفيها may mean the town's chiefs.
rows.anchor: الثاني : رؤساؤها , قاله علي بن عيسى

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: مترفيها may mean the town's morally corrupt people.
rows.anchor: الثالث : فساقها , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن أبي أوفى
rows.claim: A generation (قرن) is said to last 120 years.
rows.anchor: أنه مائة وعشرون سنة , قاله عبد الله بن أبي أوفى

rows.speaker: عبد الله بن بسر المازني
rows.claim: A generation (قرن) is alternatively said to last 100 years.
rows.anchor: أنه مائة سنة , قاله عبد الله بن بسر المازني

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet gives a generation's duration as 40 years.
rows.anchor: أنه أربعون سنة , روى ذلك محمد بن سيرين عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In worldly life, God supplies both groups, righteous and wicked; the verse does not promise this provision in the afterlife.
rows.anchor: يعني البر والفاجر من عطاء ربك في الدنيا دون الآخرة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: محظورا may mean diminished or reduced.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : منقوصا , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Alternatively, محظورا means withheld or forbidden.
rows.anchor: الثاني : ممنوعا , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة
rows.claim: Here قضى means 'commanded.'
rows.anchor: معناه وأمر ربك , قاله ابن عباس والحسن وقتادة

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Ibn Masud and Ubay read وصى ('charged/commanded'); al-Dahhak reports this reading and says the manuscript originally had it before a scribe joined the wāw to form وقضى.
rows.anchor: يقرآن { ووصى ربك } قاله الضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good treatment of parents means dutiful kindness in both deeds and speech.
rows.anchor: يعني أن يحسن إليهما بالبر بهما في الفعل والقول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One reading takes the parents' old age as coinciding with the child's full maturity and sound judgment.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : يبلغن كبرك وكما عقلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means that one or both parents reach old age through weakness and senility.
rows.anchor: الثاني : يبلغان كبرهما بالضعف والهرم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A child should not show irritation when caring for parents, as they cared for the child without irritation when young.
rows.anchor: كما كانا يميطانه عنك وأنت صغير من غير ضجر

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: أف may stand for any harsh or ugly expression.
rows.anchor: أنه كل ما غلظ من الكلام وقبح , قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: أف may express disgust at something or its odor.
rows.anchor: أنه استقذار الشيء وتغير الرائحة , قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: أف may be a sound-symbolic word expressing irritation or impatience.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنها كلمة تدل على التبرم والضجر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Arabs also pair أف and تف: the former is nail dirt and the latter something lowly picked up from the ground.
rows.anchor: والعرب أف وتف , فالأف وسخ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: قولا كريما may mean gentle speech.
rows.anchor: قولا كريما } فيه وجهان : أحدهما : لينا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means good or gracious speech.
rows.anchor: لينا . والآخر : حسنا

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that this verse and the following verse were revealed concerning Saad ibn Abi Waqqas.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس : نزلت هذه الآية والآية التي بعدها في سعد بن أبي وقاص

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Al-awwābūn are the people who do good.
rows.anchor: أحدها : أنهم المحسنون ، وهذا قول قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن المنكدر
rows.claim: Al-awwābūn are those who pray between the sunset and night prayers; Ibn al-Munkadir raises this report to the Prophet.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنهم الذين يصلون بين المغرب والعشاء ، وهذا قول ابن المنكدر يرفعه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-awwābūn are those who perform the forenoon prayer; al-Mawardi attributes this view to Awn al-Uqayli.
rows.anchor: الثالث : هم الذي يصلون الضحى

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد
rows.claim: Al-awwābūn are those who return from their sin and repent.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول سعيد بن جبير ومجاهد

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب
rows.claim: Al-awwābūn repeatedly repent, hastening back to repentance after each sin.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول سعيد بن المسيب

rows.speaker: الحسن ومجاهد
rows.claim: If unable to give a petitioner, one may turn him away while awaiting God's provision, promising future good and answering graciously.
rows.anchor: عدهم خيرا ورد عليهم ردا جميلا , وهذا قول الحسن ومجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Alternatively, a person may withhold money for fear it will be spent in disobedience, hoping for mercy for the asker; the response should still be gentle and easy.
rows.anchor: أي لينا سهلا , وهذا قول ابن زيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prohibition addresses burying daughters alive out of fear of poverty.
rows.anchor: يعني وأد البنات أحياء خيفة الفقر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The source distinguishes خطء as deliberate departure from what is right and خطأ as an inadvertent departure.
rows.anchor: والخطء العدول عن الصواب بعمد , والخطأ العدول عنه بسهو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second distinction is that خطء is sinful whereas خطأ carries no sin; Hasan reads the word with a lengthened alif.
rows.anchor: أن الخطء ما كان إثما , والخطأ ما لا إثم فيه , وقرأ الحسن خطاء بالمد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet's line calls خطء a grave offense, giving poetic support for the sinful sense.
rows.anchor: الخطء فاحشة والبر نافلة كعجوة غرست في الأرض تؤتبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Killing is lawful only on a ground that makes the victim liable to execution.
rows.anchor: يعني إلا بما تستحق به القتل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The heir's authority means the right of retaliatory execution.
rows.anchor: أنه القود , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك
rows.claim: The heir may choose retaliation, blood money, or pardon.
rows.anchor: أنه الخيار بين القود أو الدية أو العفو , وهذا قول ابن عباس والضحاك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A further interpretation is that God gives the heir authority to support and vindicate his right.
rows.anchor: فقد جعلنا لوليه سلطانا ينصره وينصفه في حقه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: One reading forbids the original killer from exceeding the bounds in killing, since the murdered person's heir will be vindicated.
rows.anchor: فلا يسرف القاتل الأول في القتل تعديا وظلما , إن ولي المقتول كان منصورا , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: طلق بن حبيب
rows.claim: The heir exceeds the bounds by killing someone other than the killer.
rows.anchor: أن يقتل غير قاتله , وهذا قول طلق بن حبيب

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: The heir exceeds the bounds by mutilating the killer when exacting retaliation.
rows.anchor: أن يمثل إذا اقتص , قاله ابن عباس

rows.speaker: يحيى
rows.claim: The heir exceeds the bounds by killing after receiving blood money.
rows.anchor: أن يقتل بعد أخذ الدية , قاله يحيى

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وداود
rows.claim: The heir exceeds the bounds by killing several people for one victim.
rows.anchor: أن يقتل جماعة بواحد , قاله سعيد بن جبير وداود

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The murdered person's heir is supported through being empowered to exact retaliation.
rows.anchor: أن الولي كان منصورا بتمكينة من القود , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Alternatively, the murdered person is supported when his killer is put to death.
rows.anchor: أن المقتول كان منصورا بقتل قاتله , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Orphans are singled out because they especially need protection and their property attracts greater greed.
rows.anchor: وإنما خص اليتيم بالذكر لأنه إلى ذلك أحوج , والطمع في ماله أكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best care may mean preserving the orphan's principal and investing its returns.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : حفظ أصوله وتثمير فروعه , وهو محتمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the best care is trading with the orphan's money for the orphan's benefit.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أن التي هي أحسن التجارة له بماله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The orphan's reaching maturity may mean reaching strength.
rows.anchor: في الأشد وجهان : أحدهما : أنه القوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means reaching the final stage of maturity.
rows.anchor: أنه القوة . الثاني : المنتهى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One view sets the age of maturity here at eighteen years.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : ثماني عشرة سنة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another view defines maturity as puberty together with sound judgment and demonstrated good sense.
rows.anchor: الثاني : الاحتلام مع سلامة العقل وإيناس الرشد

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الطبري
rows.claim: Keeping a covenant means fulfilling binding agreements between contracting parties.
rows.anchor: يلزمهم الوفاء بها , وهذا قول أبي جعفر الطبري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the covenant is the commitment in a bequest concerning an orphan's property.
rows.anchor: أنه العهد في الوصية بمال اليتيم يلزم الوفاء به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view includes everything God commands or forbids among binding covenants.
rows.anchor: كل ما أمر الله تعالى به أو نهى فهو من العهد الذي يلزم الوفاء به

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: The covenant being questioned means that it is sought or demanded.
rows.anchor: أن العهد كان مطلوبا , قاله السدي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the person who made the covenant and broke it is questioned about it.
rows.anchor: أن العهد كان مسئولا عنه الذي عهد به , فيكون ناقض العهد هو المسئول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third view makes the covenant itself answer why it was broken, by analogy with the question to the buried infant girl.
rows.anchor: أن العهد نفسه هو المسئول بم نقضت , كما تسأل الموءودة بأي ذنب قتلت

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Qistās may mean the large balance scale (القَبَّان).
rows.anchor: أنه القبان . قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Alternatively, it is any scale, large or small.
rows.anchor: أنه الميزان صغر أو كبر , وهذا قول الزجاج

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: A third meaning is justice; Mujahid regards the word as Greek.
rows.anchor: أحدهما : أنه رومي , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن درستويه
rows.claim: Alternatively, qistās means justice and is an Arabic word derived from قسط.
rows.anchor: أنه عربي مشتق من القسط , قاله ابن درستويه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Better interpretation may distinguish the outward good from the inward good.
rows.anchor: أحسن باطنا فيكون الخير ما ظهر , وحسن التأويل ما بطن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the phrase means a better outcome, since the consequence is the ultimate end of a thing.
rows.anchor: أحسن عقابة , تأويل الشيء عاقبته

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: One explanation forbids asserting that one saw, heard, or knew something when one did not.
rows.anchor: ولا علمت ولم تعلم . وهذا قول قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A second explanation forbids accusing anyone without knowledge; a Prophetic saying uses the verb for accusing one's mother and disowning one's father.
rows.anchor: هذا قول ابن عباس . ومنه قول النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation connects the verb with qiyāfa, following tracks, and cites poetry using التقافيا to mean mutual accusation.
rows.anchor: قال الشاعر : ومثل الدمى شم العرنين ساكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person may be held responsible for how he uses hearing, sight, and heart in obedience or disobedience.
rows.anchor: عن السمع والبصر والفؤاد لأنه يعمل بها إلى الطاعة والمعصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, hearing, sight, and heart themselves testify for or against a person concerning his deeds.
rows.anchor: ليكونوا شهودا عليه ، وله ، بما فعل من طاعة وما ارتكب من معصية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The plural أولئك can refer to things other than people, as Jarir's verse applies it to days.
rows.anchor: كما قال جرير : ذم المنازل بعد منزلة اللوى … والعيش بعد أولئك الأيام

none: The segment contains only an opening brace and no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marah may mean excessive joy in falsehood.
rows.anchor: أن المرح شدة الفرح بالباطل

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Marah may mean swaggering while walking.
rows.anchor: أنه الخيلاء في المشي , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marah may mean conceit and insolent exuberance.
rows.anchor: أنه البطر والأشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marah may mean a person exceeding his proper limits.
rows.anchor: أنه تجاوز الإنسان قدره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Marah may mean pride in one's manner of walking.
rows.anchor: الخامس : التكبر في المشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earth-and-mountain image may be literal: one cannot split the ground beneath one's feet or reach the mountains, so prideful excess achieves nothing.
rows.anchor: إنك لن تخرق الأرض من تحت قدمك ولن تبلغ الجبال طولا بتطاولك زجرا له عن تجاوزه الذي لا يدرك به غرضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the image is a metaphor: just as one cannot reach earth's depth or mountain height, pride cannot attain one's ambitions.
rows.anchor: أنه مثل ضربه الله تعالى له , ومعناه كما أنك لن تخرق الأرض في مشيك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sense of ṣarrafnā is that God repeated admonitions and parables throughout the Quran.
rows.anchor: كررنا في هذا القرآن من المواعظ والأمثال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, God varied the admonitions by using different kinds.
rows.anchor: غايرنا بين المواعظ باختلاف أنواعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The purpose may be for people to recall the proofs.
rows.anchor: فيه وجهان : أحدهما : ليذكروا الأدلة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the purpose is that they be guided to the truth.
rows.anchor: الثاني : ليهتدوا إلى الحق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their aversion may be aversion from the truth and following it.
rows.anchor: نفورا عن الحق والاتباع له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, they turn away from reflection and taking heed.
rows.anchor: الثاني : عن النظر والاعتبار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The syntax contains an omitted object: God varied or repeated the examples in the Quran.
rows.anchor: وفي الكلام مضمر محذوف , وتقديره ولقد صرفنا الأمثال في هذا القرآن

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: If the alleged gods were partners, they would seek a path to the Lord of the Throne through which they could reach Him.
rows.anchor: لطلبوا إليه طريقا يتصلون به لأنهم شركاء ؛ قاله سعيد بن جبير

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Alternatively, they would seek a way to draw near to God because they are beneath Him.
rows.anchor: ليتقربوا إليه لأنهم دونه , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Only living things glorify God; nonliving things do not.
rows.anchor: فأما ما ليس بحي فلا , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: إبراهيم
rows.claim: Every created thing, living or not—even a door's creak—glorifies God.
rows.anchor: حتى صرير الباب , قاله إبراهيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, creation's subtle workmanship and wondrous power, beyond human imitation, prompt observers to glorify and sanctify God.
rows.anchor: لطيف صنعته وبديع قدرته الذي يعجز الخلق عن مثله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An unnamed poet depicts creation's beauty prompting praise wherever the observer turns, supporting the sign-based interpretation.
rows.anchor: كما قال الشاعر : تلقي بتسبيحة من حيثما انصرفت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran may itself be a veil protecting the Prophet from those who reject the afterlife when he recites it.
rows.anchor: أي جعلنا القرآن حجابا ليسترك عنهم إذا قرأته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the Quran is a veil that screens disbelievers from hearing it when recited aloud.
rows.anchor: جعلنا القرآن حجابا يسترهم عن سماعه إذا جهرت به

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: On the second interpretation, their turning away makes them as if a veil stood between them and the Prophet, preventing sight.
rows.anchor: في عدم رؤيتك . قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Alternatively, the hidden veil is God's sealing their hearts so they cannot understand the Quran.
rows.anchor: حتى لا يفقهوه , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: The verse was revealed about people who harassed the Prophet at night while he recited; God shielded him from their harm.
rows.anchor: في الليل إذا قرأ , فحال الله بينه وبينهم من الأذى , قاله الزجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: مستور may mean a veil that is hidden from the listeners' sight.
rows.anchor: أن الحجاب مستور عنكم لا ترونه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, مستور means a covering veil that hides what lies behind it.
rows.anchor: أن الحجاب ساتر عنكم ما وراءه , ويكون مستور بمعنى ساتر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says the verse was revealed concerning Banu Abd al-Dar.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها نزلت في بني عبد الدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One explanation identifies the secret consultation as what the Meccans discussed at Dar al-Nadwa about the Prophet.
rows.anchor: ما تشاوروا عليه في أمر النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم في دار الندوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, Quraysh, including al-Walid ibn al-Mughira, whispered about ways to repel people from following the Prophet.
rows.anchor: كانوا يتناجون بما ينفرون به الناس عن اتباعه صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says their whispering branded the Prophet insane, a magician, and a teller of ancient fables.
rows.anchor: قال قتادة : وكانت نجواهم أنه مجنون , وأنه ساحر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One sense of مسحور is that he was bewitched and his affairs became confused, as an accusation meant to deter people.
rows.anchor: أنه سحر فاختلط عليه أمره , يقولون ذلك تنفيرا عنه

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid interprets مسحور as deceived or deluded.
rows.anchor: أن معنى مسحور مخدوع , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu Ubayda reads it as having a سحر (lung), meaning the Prophet eats and drinks like other humans and is not an angel; Labid's verse supports that lexical sense.
rows.anchor: فهو مثلكم وليس بملك , قاله أبو عبيدة

none: The segment contains only an opening brace and no commentary.

rows.speaker: الكلبي والفراء
rows.claim: رفاتا may mean dust or soil.
rows.anchor: أن الرفات التراب , قاله الكلبي والفراء

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Alternatively, it means what has crumbled from bones, like fragments; a rajaz line is cited as evidence.
rows.anchor: من العظام مثل الفتات , قاله أبو عبيدة

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر الطبري
rows.claim: The challenge to become stone or iron answers those who marvel at God recreating flesh and bones: even in those forms, they can be resurrected.
rows.anchor: إن قدرتم , قاله أبو جعفر الطبري

rows.speaker: علي بن عيسى
rows.claim: Even if people were stone or iron they could not escape God's will; the command form makes the compulsion more forceful.
rows.anchor: لم تفوتوا الله تعالى إذا أرادكم إلا أنه أخرجه مخرج الأمر لأنه أبلغ من الإلزام , قاله علي بن عيسى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A third explanation is that God would cause them to die and then bring them back to life even if they were stone or iron.
rows.anchor: لو كنتم حجارة أو حديدا لأماتكم الله ثم أحياكم

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: What seems too great may be the heavens, earth, and mountains, because of their magnitude in people's minds.
rows.anchor: السموات والأرض والجبال لعظمها في النفوس , قاله مجاهد

rows.speaker: ابن عمر وابن عباس وعبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: It may instead mean death, the most fearsome thing in a person's mind; Umayya ibn Abi al-Salt's verse describes its terror.
rows.anchor: وهذا قول ابن عمر وابن عباس وعبد الله بن عمرو بن العاص

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Another interpretation is the resurrection, which was the greatest thing in their minds.
rows.anchor: أنه أراد البعث لأنه كان أكبر شيء في صدروهم قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The phrase may include anything in creation that people regard as immense: God can still kill, revive, and resurrect them.
rows.anchor: فإن الله يميتكم ثم يحييكم ثم يبعثكم , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وقتادة
rows.claim: Nodding the head means moving it in mockery and denial; a poem illustrates the nodding motion.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس وقتادة , أي يحركون رؤوسهم استهزاء وتكذيبا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's call may be a spoken summons heard by all, calling them out to the gathering place.
rows.anchor: أنه نداء كلام يسمعه جميع الناس يدعوهم الله بالخروج فيه إلى أرض المحشر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, it may be a blast they hear that summons them to assemble on the Resurrection ground.
rows.anchor: أنها الصيحة التي يسمعونها فتكون داعية لهم إلى الاجتماع في أرض القيامة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Responding with praise may mean that they verbally praise God.
rows.anchor: فتستجيبون حامدين لله تعالى بألسنتكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, their response may occur through actions that merit praise of God.
rows.anchor: فتستجيبون على ما يقتضي حمد الله من أفعالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading is that they rise from their graves praising God rather than themselves.
rows.anchor: معناه فستقومون من قبوركم بحمد الله لا بحمد أنفسكم

rows.speaker: سفيان وابن جريج
rows.claim: Alternatively, they respond by God's command.
rows.anchor: فتستجيبون بأمره , قاله سفيان وابن جريج

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: They think they remained only briefly in worldly life because the afterlife is so long.
rows.anchor: أحدها : إن لبثتم إلا قليلا في الدنيا لطول لبثكم في الآخرة , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: The phrase can express how insignificant worldly life seems when they see the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: الثاني : معناه الاحتقار لأمر الدنيا حين عاينوا يوم القيامة , قاله قتادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The speed with which they return from death makes them think their time in the graves was brief.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنهم لما يرون من سرعة الرجوع يظنون قلة اللبث في القبور

rows.speaker: الكلبي
rows.claim: Another view is the forty years between trumpet blasts, when punishment is lifted; relief makes that interval seem short.
rows.anchor: وبينهما أربعون سنة فيرونها لاستراحتهم قليقلة ؛ قاله الكلبي

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: It may simply indicate the nearness of the time, as in the saying that the world seems never to have existed while the afterlife seems always present.
rows.anchor: كما قال الحسن كأنك بالدنيا لم تكن وبالآخرة لم تزل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One meaning of telling servants to speak in the best way is affirming the Prophet's message; Satan incites them to deny him.
rows.anchor: أنه تصديق النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فيما جاء به

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: The phrase may mean carrying out God's commands and avoiding His prohibitions.
rows.anchor: الثاني : أنه امتثال أوامر الله تعالى ونواهيه , قاله الحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another interpretation is to command what is right and forbid what is wrong.
rows.anchor: الثالث : أنه الأمر بالمعروف والنهي عن المنكر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It may mean answering someone who insults you with a good reply.
rows.anchor: الرابع : أن يرد خيرا على من شتمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A reported occasion says the verse came down when a Quraysh unbeliever insulted Umar and Umar moved to retaliate.
rows.anchor: وقيل إنها نزلت في عمر بن الخطاب رضي الله عنه وقد شتمه رجل من بعض كفار قريش
